intro: Case Converter changes text between camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, kebab-case, CONSTANT_CASE, Title Case, Sentence case, lowercase and UPPERCASE. It splits your input into words by detecting camelCase boundaries, underscores, hyphens and whitespace, then re-joins them in the case style you pick. It is handy when renaming variables, generating identifiers, or normalizing strings across a codebase.
useCases: Convert a variable name from snake_case to camelCase or PascalCase when moving code between languages
Turn a phrase or heading into a kebab-case slug for URLs or file names
Generate CONSTANT_CASE names for environment variables or enum members
Reformat database column names into Title Case or Sentence case labels for a UI
Quickly switch a block of text to all lowercase or UPPERCASE
Normalize mixed-style identifiers (spaces, dashes, underscores) into one consistent case

faq.q: Is my data sent to a server?
faq.a: No. The conversion runs entirely in your browser with JavaScript, and nothing you type is uploaded or stored remotely.
camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, kebab-case, CONSTANT_CASE, Title Case, Sentence case, lowercase and UPPERCASE.

faq.q: How does it decide where words begin and end?
faq.a: It treats a lowercase-to-uppercase transition (like myValue), underscores, hyphens, and whitespace as word boundaries, then collapses repeated separators.

faq.q: How are numbers and acronyms handled?
faq.a: Numbers stay attached to the word they follow rather than starting a new word, and acronyms are not detected specially, so a run of capitals like 'JSONData' is split only at the J-to-S style boundary, which may not match your expectation for all-caps groups.

faq.q: What do lowercase and UPPERCASE modes do differently?
faq.a: Unlike the other styles, lowercase and UPPERCASE do not re-split into words; they simply change the case of the entire input while keeping spaces and punctuation as-is.
